class.name: PhysXWaterSurface3D
class.brief_description: A real animated water surface: a GPU FFT ocean spectrum layer plus a local ripple layer that bodies can disturb, rendered as a displaced mesh.
class.description: Two coupled simulation layers, both real-time GPU compute through the shared main [RenderingDevice] when windowed: a local iWave-style ripple layer (a damped 2D wave equation you can disturb via [method submit_sphere]/[method submit_impulse]) and a Tessendorf FFT ocean spectrum layer (large-scale wind-driven chop, tuned by [member wind_speed]/[member wind_direction]/[member wave_amplitude]). Rendering also produces optional light-space caustics with a direct [RenderingDevice] graphics pass; it does not create a second [SubViewport]. A child [MeshInstance3D] (a subdivided [PlaneMesh], sized to [member ocean_domain_size], or the resampled [member surface_mesh] footprint) is created automatically and displaced by both layers, summed. Call [method sample_height] to query the same combined surface on the CPU -- e.g. from a buoyancy script (see [code]demo/common/buoyant_body.gd[/code] in the paired demo project) -- and [method submit_sphere] once per physics tick per floating body so it actually disturbs the ripple layer, not just receives a height back. No [RenderingDevice] compute support (e.g. running headless) leaves the surface flat and [method sample_height] returning [member water_level] plus zero -- a graceful no-op, not an error, matching every other GPU solver in this module. Set [member surface_mesh] to give the water any outline -- a round pool, a kidney-bean pond, a lake with an island. Waves reflect off its shoreline, and [method sample_height]/[method is_wet] report no water outside it. Set [member seabed_from_floor] for water over uneven ground -- a beach, a lake bed. The still-water depth of every ripple cell is then measured from the floor: waves travel at the local shallow-water speed, so they slow and bunch up over shallows, the shoreline falls wherever the ground rises above the water, and the ocean chop fades out over the last [member shallow_fade_depth] metres. Without it, the whole surface uses the constant [member depth]. Both simulation grids are centred on the node's global position (plus the [member surface_mesh] footprint's centre), fixed when the node enters the tree or a property changes. The node's rotation and scale are not applied to the simulation, so keep it unrotated and unscaled. Only runs in an actual running game, never in the editor -- placing or moving the node in the Inspector does not simulate.

method.name: get_caustics_texture
method.description: The zero-copy caustics light-pattern texture. Project a receiving surface's world position onto [method get_caustics_light_right] and [method get_caustics_light_up], relative to [method get_caustics_origin], and map the result through [method get_caustics_half_extent] to sample the texture. Null until [member caustics_enabled] is true and the node has built.

method.name: get_caustics_half_extent
method.description: Half-width of the square light-space projection in world units, used to map receiver positions to [method get_caustics_texture] UV coordinates.

method.name: get_caustics_light_right
method.description: Light-space horizontal projection axis used to sample [method get_caustics_texture].

method.name: get_caustics_light_up
method.description: Light-space vertical projection axis used to sample [method get_caustics_texture].

method.name: get_caustics_origin
method.description: World-space center of the light-space caustics projection.

method.name: clear_sphere
method.description: Removes a previously-submitted sphere proxy (see [method submit_sphere]) by its owner id. Call this when a floating body leaves the water or is freed; a proxy left in place otherwise keeps disturbing the ripple layer at its last submitted position.

method.name: is_wet
method.description: Whether [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ lies inside the [member surface_mesh] footprint, at the ripple grid's resolution. Always [code]true[/code] when no [member surface_mesh] is set. [code]world_pos.y[/code] is ignored.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: The combined surface height (ripple + ocean layers, plus [member water_level]) at [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ, bilinearly sampled from the last periodic readback (a few frames behind the GPU simulation -- fine for buoyancy, not meant for sub-frame precision). [code]world_pos.y[/code] is ignored. Returns [code]-INF[/code] where [method is_wet] is [code]false[/code] (outside the [member surface_mesh] footprint), so anything comparing a point's height against it -- a buoyancy script's submersion depth -- reads "not in water" there.

method.name: submit_impulse
method.description: A one-shot local disturbance (a splash) at [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ -- consumed by the next simulation step, then cleared automatically. Call it once per event (e.g. on impact), not every tick.

method.name: submit_sphere
method.description: A persistent body proxy that pushes the ripple layer's surface down near [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ, proportional to [code]radius[/code] and [code]strength[/code]. Call once per physics tick while a body is in the water (e.g. from its own [code]_physics_process[/code]), keyed by any id stable for that body's lifetime -- [code]get_instance_id()[/code] works well. Call [method clear_sphere] with the same id when the body leaves.

members.member: Approximate distance the refracted light travels below the surface before it is mapped into the caustics texture. Larger values spread the pattern farther sideways for oblique light.
Enables the light-space caustics draw pass and its render target. When disabled, the extra GPU buffers and draw are skipped. See [method get_caustics_texture].
World-space direction that light travels from the source toward the water. It need not be normalized.

Tessendorf horizontal displacement of the ocean layer: pulls the surface toward the wave crests so they sharpen and the troughs flatten, the way real wind waves look. [code]0[/code] is a pure height field; around [code]1[/code] is realistic, and much higher can fold the surface through itself. Fades out over the shallows with the rest of the ocean chop. Where the displacement squeezes the surface the default material draws whitecap foam (its [code]foam_threshold[/code] and [code]foam_color[/code] shader parameters tune it). [method sample_height] accounts for the displacement.
Damping (ALPHA) on the local ripple layer's wave equation -- higher settles disturbances faster.

Still-water depth in metres used everywhere unless [member seabed_from_floor] measures it per cell (then it only applies where no floor is found below the water). Sets the ripple layer's wave speed, [code]sqrt(g * depth)[/code], and the ocean layer's dispersion.

World-space extent (X, Z) of the local ripple layer -- independent of [member ocean_domain_size], see [member ocean_grid_resolution]'s own note on why. Ignored when [member surface_mesh] is set: the ripple grid is then fitted to the footprint's bounds.

How far the wind has blown over open water, in metres. The ocean layer is a fetch-limited JONSWAP spectrum, so fetch sets how tall and how long the wind waves get at a given [member wind_speed]: a few metres give tiny, short ripples, kilometres give a developed sea. [code]0[/code] (auto) uses the [member surface_mesh] footprint's longest side for enclosed water, or a fully developed open sea (100 km) without one. Only wavelengths up to [member ocean_domain_size] are represented, and waves shorter than two ocean grid cells aren't, so a small fetch at a coarse [member ocean_grid_resolution] can leave the ocean layer flat.
Cell count per side of the local ripple layer's grid. Not required to be a power of two, unlike [member ocean_grid_resolution].

How the surface's normals and whitecap foam are computed, set on the material through its [code]per_pixel_normals[/code] uniform. [constant NORMAL_MODE_PER_PIXEL] uses the exact slopes and displacement derivatives the ocean FFT also produces ([code]ocean_deriv_tex[/code]), so crests shade smoothly and foam follows the folds at any mesh density -- the realistic choice. [constant NORMAL_MODE_PER_VERTEX] takes finite differences of the displaced mesh, so the shading follows the mesh -- softer, faceted at a coarse [member ocean_grid_resolution], for a stylized look.
World-space extent (X, Z) of the FFT ocean layer -- also the size of the rendered [PlaneMesh].

Cell count per side of the FFT ocean layer's grid. Rounded up to the nearest power of two if set otherwise -- the Stockham FFT passes require it. Independent of [member grid_resolution]/[member domain_size] (the ripple layer's own grid) by design: they're two different consumers of "water height" with very different resolution/precision needs, kept architecturally separate rather than forced to share one grid.
Multiplier on the ripple displacement driven by submitted floating-body proxies and impulses. Set lower for small splashes and wakes in a pool; this does not scale the FFT ocean waves.
Physics layers [member seabed_from_floor]'s rays hit. Only static bodies count; a rigid or character body in the way is skipped.

When on, the still-water depth of each ripple cell is measured on the first physics tick by a ray straight down onto the static bodies in [member seabed_collision_mask], starting 100 m above the water. Waves then travel at the local shallow-water speed, cells where the floor is above the water are dry shore ([method sample_height] returns [code]-INF[/code] and [method is_wet] [code]false[/code] there), and the ocean chop fades out over the shallows (see [member shallow_fade_depth]). Where no floor is found the constant [member depth] applies. Combines with [member surface_mesh]: cells outside its footprint stay dry. The floor is measured once; moving it afterwards needs a property change to re-measure.

Water shallower than this many metres fades the ocean chop out, down to none at the waterline, so the surface meets a beach calmly instead of the chop cutting through the sand. Only has an effect where the depth varies ([member seabed_from_floor] or [member surface_mesh]).

Optional water outline: any flat [Mesh] (node-local) whose up-facing triangles' X/Z footprint is the water -- e.g. a disc baked from a [CSGCylinder3D], or a shape modelled elsewhere. Its own vertices are not displaced directly; the footprint is resampled into an even grid clipped to the outline, so a coarse or fan-triangulated mesh still gets vertices to animate everywhere. When set, the ripple grid is fitted to the footprint's bounds ([member domain_size] is ignored) at [member grid_resolution], cells outside it are dry land the waves reflect off, caustics are cut to the water area, and [method sample_height] returns [code]-INF[/code] over dry cells. The FFT ocean layer still covers [member ocean_domain_size] around the same centre -- size it to cover the footprint. Unset, the water is the square [member domain_size] / [member ocean_domain_size] plane.
Mean world-space Y of the surface -- place the node here rather than relying on its own transform, since the rendered mesh and both simulation layers are displaced relative to this baseline.

The material driving the surface mesh's displacement/shading. A default is created automatically if left unset -- assign your own only if you need to customize the look; it must keep sampling [code]ripple_height_tex[/code]/[code]ocean_height_tex[/code] in its vertex shader the same way the default does, or the mesh will stop moving.

Linear height multiplier for the FFT ocean waves. At [code]1.0[/code] they have physical heights for the JONSWAP spectrum at [member wind_speed] and [member fetch] (in metres); below 1 reduces them proportionally, 0 removes the FFT ocean waves. This does not scale local ripple disturbances.
Direction (X, Z) the wind blows toward; the FFT ocean waves are aligned with it and travel downwind. Need not be normalized.
Wind speed in m/s driving the FFT ocean layer's spectrum -- higher produces longer, larger waves, up to what [member fetch] allows.

constants.constant: Normals and foam per pixel from the ocean FFT's exact derivatives.
Normals and foam per vertex from finite differences of the displaced mesh.
